summary:
# NOTES: E. V. Lucas, *London Lavender* (1912), compact reference

Single book. Narrator: Kent Falconer, honorary secretary to a folk-song society, living with wife Naomi at 7 Primrose Terrace, Regent's Park (landladies: Misses Laura and Emma Packer, twins; Mrs. Wiles, their help). Daughter Lavender "Nan" born ch. XXXV. Final chapter: move to a house with a garden, Lavender asleep.

## Cast (key)
- **Falconer, Kent** (narrator); **Naomi** (wife; daughter of Mr. Wynne; sister Mrs. Frank Wynne).
- **Lavender "Nan" Falconer**: born 3:15 A.M., rainy morning. Name debate: Placida (Kent) vs Lavender (Naomi); nickname Nan.
- **Wiles, Mordecai**: head keeper, New Ape House, Zoo. Ourang-outang Barbara (his favourite). Wife **Susan**, former Packers' help. Inherit £50,000 (will of uncle Samuel Wiles, 18 Bonchurch Road, Melbourne; £2000/yr; cheque £500; firm Morgan & Rice). Move to a house off Camden Town Road. Adopt chimpanzee "Lou" (dies); later adopt baby **Annie** (orphan; father killed by motor-bus). Wiles to be set up in a chop-house.
- **Lacey, Nathan**: first-floor-back; impulsive, generous, "frankest man"; secretary to an art club; cold/hot chop-house scheme; helps Wiles, Duckie. Organ-grinder episode (one-legged organist). Helps prostitute-ish girl found in Russell Square; sends her to Dimmage's (old carpenter; wife Mrs. Dimmage).
- **Furley, Sam**: first-floor-front; cinema film maker; farm in Essex; sneeze film idea "The Fatal Sneeze"/"Mr. Splodgers"; sends Kent 100 cigars.
- **Spanton, Robert**: top-floor-back; young Socialist; manual labour scheme; engaged to **Nancy Freeland** (breaks off, ch. XXVI). Opposes Lacey's charity.
- **Carstairs, John** (alias of James Murchison): top-floor-front; recluse; reformed thief; stole Verrocchio portrait (small Madonna; girl's head) from National Gallery; dies; leaves estate to National Art Collections Fund; executor Kent (£500); Kent returns picture via Piccadilly Circus Tube cloak-room; Times article. Buried at Kensal Green; epitaph "O thou fairest among women."
- **Miss Cole**: spinster rentier, gossip. **Misses Packer**: Laura (older by half an hour), Emma; father a bank messenger.
- **Dabney, Mr.**: editor of *The Balance*; rooms in King's Bench Walk; housewarming with Rudson-Wayte (politician; cynic), young politician speaker.
- **Duckie, John** (waiter) and **Martha** (wife, Mrs. Duckie): former Bemerton's servants. Children Beatrice ("Lazie Glee") and Ern ("The Four Uglies"). Duckie wants eating-house; Gog and Magog Chop House. Mrs. Duckie's devastating remark: "you could die to-morrow... You've got 'one child only' written all over you."
- **Bemerton, Joseph**: second-hand bookseller; lends privately printed book (Miss A.'s village conversations: Mary Powell, Anne Williams, Ned (stonemason), David (Welsh widower)).
- **Heathcote, Adolphus "Dollie"**: young man about town; motor-cars; "Wow, wow!"; engaged to **Ann Ingleside** (daughter of **Sir Gaston Ingleside**, civil servant, K.C.B.). Secret registry marriage (ring cost £3 10s); winning horse Decree Nisi 20-1. Ann's sister Alison in Ceylon.
- **Farrar, Algernon** (Algy), young motorist; wife **Gwendolen** (Gwen), daughter of Canon Frome's circle; trip to Winfield; Harberton family (Lynn, Edith; three girls; Boswell editor).
- **Director, The**: folk-song collector; Mowing the Barley, Wraggle Taggle Gipsies, Winter's Signs, Sussex hunting songs.
- **Freelands** (Mr. Freeland, Mrs. Freeland; daughters Jocelyn, Mona, Joan, Janet, Phillida, Nancy); Whisky the Aberdeen terrier; Freeland's green jodhpur hat, tall hat / straw hat story.
- **Millionaire-novelists at Dabney's**: Devon (urbane reformer), Speyde (analyst), Leigh (sentimental humorist), Sankville (provincial epics).
- **Miss Mitt**: Warden of Pink Almshouses (13 houses, 12 old women, 10s/wk). Residents: Selina Still, Gipsy Woods, Mrs. Nottidge gin/tea story, Martha Drax (writing letter to King on alcohol).
- **Eli and Jack Hayes**: ancient Morris dancers, Oxfordshire (Bicester); Muggeridge pipe and tabor player; Eli 70.
- **Uncle Jonah Surely**: Sussex shepherd; Quaker master Mr. Willing; Raikes interest penny; Low Bottom barn birth; lamb toll "fippence a score."
- **Rimini** (ch. XXII–XXV): Wynne family (Frank, Mrs. Frank, three children incl. twins, Jill); Golden Eagle and Three Kings hotel; Englishman bathing attendant ("awry," "ole man"); Ravenna (Dante, Byron, Hotel Byron); San Marino (wasted day, republic); Prue story; mosquitoes.
- **Sir Gaston's card trick**: picked winner and second with eyes closed; Derby (Paladin, Peppermint, Witch Hazel, Palimpsest, Crumpet; grey filly won; Kent bet 4 pounds on favourite (unnamed?) and 3 pounds each way on Peppermint; Ratton's mount).
- **Glenister/Bradley/Goat story** (Sir Gaston's Irish youth; butler Rice; Blackadder; butler bolted).

## Chapter-by-chapter events
- I: Move to Primrose Terrace. Mrs. Wiles's ape/monkey definition.
- II: Tenants Carstairs, Spanton, Furley, Lacey. Organ-grinder quarrel; police notice.
- III: Wiles and Barbara; Zoo tour (wombat, capuchin, giraffes, elephant, otter).
- IV: Kent becomes honorary secretary; folk songs ("Mowing the Barley," "Wraggle Taggle Gipsies").
- V: Dollie and Ann lunch; telephone-reversal story (dead man's voice).
- VI: Lacey introduced (cat on step); chop restaurant idea; samplers.
- VII: Dabney's housewarming; Rudson-Wayte.
- VIII: Wiles inheritance; Wiles left Zoo; adoption suggested.
- IX: Spanton's Socialist scheme; interchange idea.
- X: Freelands; Spanton and Nancy; garden-party tall hat story.
- XI: Wiles adopts chimp Lou; "Not now" motto (No Cross, no Crown).
- XII: Furley's film studio; cinema industry.
- XIII: Mrs. Duckie; Miss A.'s book.
- XIV–XVII: Derby; Dollie's betting; Sir Gaston's Irish gambling story; Sussex songs (XVIII); cinema sneeze (XIX).
- XX–XXI: Novelists at Dabney's; Lacey and girl (Dimmage's); Christianity argument.
- XXII–XXV: Rimini trip; Prue story; Ravenna and San Marino.
- XXVI: Dollie and Spanton (Nancy breaks engagement).
- XXVII: Ormond Wall face story (told by little pale man, fabrication).
- XXVIII: Oxfordshire Morris dancers (Eli, Jack; "We be the last").
- XXIX: Naomi pregnant; name Lavender chosen; "Nan."
- XXX: Motor trip to Winfield; actor (half-crown); Harbertons.
- XXXI: Almshouses; Martha Drax story.
- XXXII–XXXIII: Carstairs' confession; Verrocchio; restitution; Times.
- XXXIV: Wiles's new opportunity (chop-house; Lacey, Duckie); Annie adopted.
- XXXV: Lavender born; Lavender lavender song.
- XXXVI: Mrs. Duckie's remark; Lacey's sunset/kinkajou talk; Kent's reflections on Nan.
- XXXVII: Dollie and Ann's secret marriage; Sir Gaston's reaction; Decree Nisi.
- Final: New house with garden; Lavender asleep.
